authority_boundary: This registry is candidate language guidance for AI coding agents. It does not override repo-local style, tests, security policy, source authority, or human gates. Frontier source intake is pointer-only until screened and validated.
evidence_methodology: Language advantages are promoted only from official or reviewed source pointers plus local validation evidence. Underuse and frontier labels are heuristic unless backed by measurement or repeated DAD outcomes; they must not gate security-sensitive actions.

languages.label: Python
frontier_questions: Which new Python versions, PEPs, typing features, diagnostics, or stdlib tools should change AI coding defaults?
Which Python idioms make code easier for future agents to inspect, validate, and safely edit?
Which property-based, static-analysis, or fixture patterns catch AI-authored edge cases before review?
Which slow Python workflows should be improved through orchestration, profiling, vectorized libraries, or a Rust shadow path?

ai_advantages.summary: Use Python's stdlib and type tools to make JSON, resource, state, and side-effect boundaries explicit before code sprawls.
use_when: A repo has schemas, JSONL, config, CLI, file I/O, or public API surfaces.
An AI agent is writing broad dictionary-heavy Python.
avoid_when: The task is a tiny disposable script.
A framework-specific model is already the local authority.
verification: Run affected tests or py_compile.
Validate JSON/schema boundaries when structured records change.
Cite py-idiom IDs when a review recommendation relies on an idiom.

ai_advantages.summary: Use profiling and test orchestration before proposing rewrites or skipping broad pytest runs.
use_when: A Python test suite is slow or full-battery runs block iteration.
A change touches isolated modules with measurable coverage boundaries.
avoid_when: A shared behavior or public contract changed and a smaller suite cannot prove coverage.
There is no structured evidence that selected tests cover the change.
verification: Record slow-test inventory and selection rationale.
Run native pytest for the selected scope and full validation before promotion.
Gate timing claims behind verified coverage evidence.

ai_advantages.summary: Use property-based tests and static checker contracts to make agent-written edge cases fail deterministically before broad review.
use_when: A function parses, normalizes, routes, deduplicates, hashes, or transforms structured records.
A public API, Protocol, TypedDict, or dataclass boundary has invariants that examples alone may miss.
avoid_when: The repo has no test budget or dependency policy for property-based tools.
The desired guarantee is runtime validation but the proposed check is only a type hint.
verification: Add at least one small invariant test or negative type-check case before promoting the tactic.
Keep generated counterexamples sanitized and local unless approved for DAD mail.
Record whether the checker or property test actually caught a defect in postflight.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: TypedDict, dataclasses, schemas, or small parser functions should mark where raw JSON becomes domain data.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: Agents often keep nested dictionaries because they are quick to write and pass smoke tests.
detection_signals: Nested dict access across multiple functions.
JSONL or config loaders without validation or domain conversion.
Repeated string keys in CLI, mail, schema, or registry code.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: Filesystem, subprocess, clock, network, and mail writes should be isolated when tests or replay matter.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: Direct side-effect calls make generated code shorter at first and hide test cost until later.
detection_signals: Business logic directly calls subprocess, Path.write_text, datetime.now, requests, or environment reads.
Tests require real files, network, or wall clock to exercise ordinary logic.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: Small property tests can protect parsers, serializers, IDs, and dedupe logic from edge cases agents do not enumerate.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: Agents usually write example tests that mirror the happy path they just implemented.
detection_signals: Round-trip, normalize, split, merge, sort, hash, or dedupe functions with only example tests.
A bug fix mentions an edge input but the regression test covers only that single input.
Mail, exception, schema, or registry code has invariants independent of specific sample records.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: When a repo already runs mypy, pyright, or similar, negative type tests can freeze API and Protocol expectations.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: AI agents tend to treat type hints as documentation and do not ask whether the type checker is an executable contract.
detection_signals: Protocols, NewType IDs, overloads, or TypedDict boundaries with no checker command.
A public API migration where wrong caller shapes should fail before runtime.
A repo has type-checker config but new guidance omits it from validation.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use Python's AST and inspection tools to ask structural questions before guessing from grep or memory.
run_or_inspect: Small repo-local ast.parse or symtable script for definitions, decorators, imports, and repeated keys.
inspect.signature and importlib.metadata for real callable and entry-point surfaces.
python -m py_compile or python -m compileall for syntax/import-time proof on changed modules.
use_when: A task changes registries, CLI surfaces, dynamic imports, generated modules, or repeated JSON keys.
Text search finds too many matches or misses runtime registration paths.
proof_output: Counts, paths, symbol names, signatures, or compile results rather than copied source bodies.
A short note explaining which assumption the structural query confirmed or falsified.
safety_limits: Do not send private source snippets through DAD mail.
Treat dynamic import results as repo-local evidence, not source authority for another repo.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use cProfile, pstats, tracemalloc, and faulthandler before declaring a Python path slow, leaky, or stuck.
run_or_inspect: python -m cProfile -o profile.out <command> followed by pstats summaries.
tracemalloc snapshots around suspected allocation-heavy paths.
faulthandler.dump_traceback_later for hangs and deadlocks in local-only debugging.
use_when: A task mentions slow tests, hot paths, memory growth, hangs, or possible Rust migration.
The suspected bottleneck might be fixture setup, subprocess waits, imports, or I/O rather than CPU.
proof_output: Command, duration, top cumulative functions, allocation summary, or stack traces sanitized to paths and symbols.
Before/after evidence on the same workload before any speed claim.
safety_limits: Do not publish raw traces if they contain private paths, arguments, secrets, or row contents.
Do not propose Rust from profiling until Python-first fixes and same-workload evidence are recorded.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use pytest collection, durations, markers, and property-test probes to map what a change actually exercises.
run_or_inspect: python -m pytest --collect-only for candidate scope.
python -m pytest --durations=<n> on the relevant suite.
Small Hypothesis/property probes for parsers, normalizers, dedupe, IDs, and serializers when locally allowed.
use_when: A test suite is too slow for every iteration.
A fix changes a class of inputs but only has example tests.
proof_output: Collected node IDs, duration summary, selected-test rationale, and invariant name.
A regression that would fail on old behavior, or a recorded reason the property tool is not approved.
safety_limits: Selected tests are evidence only when scope is explained.
Generated counterexamples stay local unless sanitized and reviewed.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Inspect the repo's actual Python version, package metadata, entry points, lock files, and configured tools before recommending tactics.
run_or_inspect: python --version and pyproject/tool sections.
importlib.metadata.version and entry_points for installed local packages.
Ruff, uv, pytest, mypy, or pyright config only when the repo already carries those tools.
use_when: A guidance item depends on a Python version, optional checker, package manager, or test plugin.
An agent is about to suggest a new dependency or tool.
proof_output: Version floor, configured tool list, and whether the repo already runs the needed command.
A local approval note before adding optional tooling.
safety_limits: Do not treat available global tools as repo-approved tools.
Do not include full environment dumps or paths in public-facing mail.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Turn raw dictionaries, JSONL rows, CLI payloads, and config blobs into named boundary objects or validated records before business logic spreads.
use_when: Code repeats string keys across functions.
A future agent must know which fields are required, optional, public-safe, or source-owned.
proof_required: A schema, TypedDict, dataclass, pydantic model, or parser function owns the boundary.
Tests or validation commands cover malformed input and missing fields.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: The agent keeps adding dict access until local tests pass, but later changes silently drift field names or source authority.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Use Python profiling, algorithmic fixes, fixture trimming, and test orchestration before proposing Rust for speed.
use_when: The task says slow, performance, full battery, parser, chunker, or hot path.
The workload may be I/O-bound, subprocess-bound, or fixture-bound rather than CPU-bound.
proof_required: A baseline command, duration, scope, and profile or slow-test inventory.
A same-workload after measurement before claiming improvement.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: Rust looks faster only because the comparison was a tiny Rust path against a broad Python suite.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Prefer checks that fail deterministically: schema validation, property tests, static checker contracts, py_compile, and small negative tests.
use_when: An API has invariants examples do not fully enumerate.
A bug fix describes a class of malformed inputs, not just one sample.
proof_required: At least one executable check that would fail on the old behavior.
A note about the repo's Python version and whether optional type/property tools are already accepted.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: The agent writes explanatory comments or type hints that look rigorous but are never executed.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Use ast, inspect, importlib.metadata, cProfile, pstats, tracemalloc, and faulthandler before guessing how unfamiliar Python behaves.
use_when: A task asks why code is slow, hanging, leaking, dynamically registered, or hard to search.
Grep gives too many false positives or misses generated/runtime registrations.
proof_required: Record the exact introspection/profiling command and what it proved.
Keep private source snippets out of DAD mail; send paths, counts, hashes, and safe summaries only.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: The agent relies on training-data assumptions instead of inspecting the repo's real callable signatures, imports, and runtime costs.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Prefer Python changes that expose named boundaries, deterministic commands, safe summaries, and small negative cases for future agents.
use_when: A future agent will need to extend, audit, or repair the code without chat context.
A module emits JSONL, reports, CLI output, schemas, exceptions, or cross-repo candidate evidence.
proof_required: The changed surface has a stable command, schema, parser, or test fixture that can be inspected without reading long raw content.
At least one negative or malformed-input path is covered when the boundary is shared.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: The code is readable to the author but leaves future agents with hidden conventions, untestable prose, or output that looks authoritative without proof.

watch_for: stdlib tools that replace hand-rolled helper code
diagnostics, typing, concurrency, and performance changes that alter good AI defaults

Treating draft PEPs as adopted rules.

example_refs.provenance_note: Official pytest project repository; pointer-only test orchestration source.
Official Hypothesis project repository; pointer-only property-testing source.
Mypy project repository; pointer-only static checker source.
Pyright project repository; pointer-only static checker source.

watch_for: fixture and collection patterns that reduce slow-suite cost
property strategies and stateful tests that expose edge cases
negative type-check patterns for APIs, Protocols, and TypedDict boundaries
codebase_watch_targets.why_ai_agents_should_study: These codebases and docs turn review opinions into executable failures, which is exactly what future agents need.
it_must_not_be_used_for: Adding dependencies to downstream repos without local approval.
Sending generated counterexamples or private test inputs through DAD mail.

codebase_watch_targets.label: Fast Python tooling implemented with Rust

example_refs.provenance_note: Official Ruff repository; pointer-only fast Python tooling source.
Official uv repository; pointer-only Python environment tooling source.
Official maturin documentation; pointer-only Python/Rust packaging source.
Official PyO3 documentation; pointer-only Python/Rust boundary source.

watch_for: CLI UX and report formats that make tooling agent-readable
Python/Rust boundary patterns that keep Python orchestration while Rust owns deterministic leaf work
packaging and environment workflows that reduce per-repo drift
codebase_watch_targets.why_ai_agents_should_study: These tools demonstrate how Rust can improve Python workflows without forcing every repo to become a Rust repo.
it_must_not_be_used_for: Assuming a Rust-backed tool is appropriate for every repo.
Claiming speed or safety benefits without local workload evidence.

intake_gate: Record pointer-only source refs, target Python version, applicability limits, and a validation idea.
Screen for copied docs, private data, licenses, dependency policy, and tool availability.
promotion_evidence: A local example, regression test, property test, type-check case, profile, or harness outcome shows the tactic helped.
At least one avoid-when or counterexample is documented.
Postflight or usage feedback records whether the tactic was used, ignored, failed, or harmful.
rejection_signals: The tactic is clever but makes code less readable under local style.
The benefit depends on optional tools the repo does not run.
The source is a draft, benchmark claim, or popularity signal with no local proof path.

harness_routes.use_when: Full pytest is slow, flaky, or not targeted enough for the active change.
A profiled Python hot path may be replaced by Rust while keeping the Python API stable.
A Python source, idiom, package, typing feature, or testing technique might become DAD guidance.
evidence_required: trusted source pointer or explicit source justification
local validation idea or command before promotion

validation_gates: Run repo-local Python tests or explain why they are unavailable.
Run schema validation when JSON, JSONL, or registry contracts change.
Run lint/type checks only when the repo already uses them or adoption is explicitly planned.
Do not claim performance savings without baseline and after timings from the same workload.
adoption_rules: Use the smallest Python feature that clarifies data shape, boundary, or validation.
Treat underused idioms as citable review prompts, not rewrite mandates.
Send useful or harmful outcomes back through dad:need:language-frontier-signals or dad:need:coding-harness-feedback.
anti_patterns: Clever Python solely to look advanced.
Skipping tests because a selected suite was fast.
Replacing Python with Rust before profiling and parity evidence exist.

languages.label: Rust
frontier_questions: Which newly stabilized Rust, Cargo, Clippy, or stdlib changes make code easier for agents to verify?
Which crates or patterns improve deterministic scanning, parsing, chunking, hashing, and static analysis for DAD?
Which fuzzing, property, or isolated test-runner patterns expose parser and parity mistakes faster than ordinary examples?
Which Python hot paths deserve a Rust shadow experiment rather than a full rewrite?

ai_advantages.summary: Use Rust where enums, newtypes, ownership, and exhaustive matching can turn future-agent mistakes into compiler errors.
use_when: A parser, classifier, or route table has closed variants and correctness-critical transitions.
Stringly typed IDs or statuses are causing drift across boundaries.
avoid_when: The code is fast-changing orchestration where Python readability and iteration speed matter more.
A local team cannot validate or maintain Rust yet.
verification: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo test, and doc tests where applicable.
Add parity tests for behavior formerly owned by Python.
Keep public API changes behind semver or human review.

ai_advantages.summary: Use Rust for profiled CPU-bound chunking, parsing, hashing, diffing, or scoring hot paths while Python keeps orchestration.
use_when: Profiling shows a real Python CPU hot loop.
The boundary can be expressed as small deterministic input/output functions.
avoid_when: The workload is I/O-bound or dominated by subprocess time.
Parity cannot be proven with structured reports.
verification: Record Python baseline timings and Rust shadow timings on the same inputs.
Require same-scope structured parity before timing claims.
Use PyO3/maturin only after the boundary is stable.

ai_advantages.summary: Design Rust parser, scanner, chunker, and serializer boundaries so fuzzing and property tests can attack them without repo-specific side effects.
use_when: A Rust module accepts untrusted text, bytes, paths, JSONL, or cross-repo metadata.
A bug class depends on edge inputs that example tests are unlikely to cover.
avoid_when: The boundary still depends on filesystem, network, clock, or Python interpreter state.
Generated corpora could contain private-source data and no sanitization plan exists.
verification: Keep the fuzz target or property test around a pure deterministic function.
Store crash or minimized examples locally unless sanitized and approved for DAD.
Record fuzz/property outcomes as harness evidence before promotion.

ai_advantages.summary: Use Rust test runner and Clippy output as structured evidence when parity, speed, or safety claims need audit trails.
use_when: A Rust shadow layer, CLI validator, or cross-repo tool needs repeatable pass/fail evidence.
A repo has many Rust tests where isolation or machine-readable output would improve triage.
avoid_when: The ordinary cargo test output is already sufficient and no audit claim depends on structure.
The test-runner dependency would add more maintenance cost than signal.
verification: Compare native cargo test and alternate runner results before changing defaults.
Capture command, exit code, duration, and report path in harness outcomes.
Do not call a run faster unless the same workload and same scope were measured.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: Represent closed packet, event, status, or parser states as enums with exhaustive matches instead of strings.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: String constants are easier to generate and look familiar from Python/JSON examples.
detection_signals: Repeated status strings in Rust or mixed Python/Rust code.
Wildcard match arms hiding unhandled variants.
JSON schema enum values manually mirrored in code.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: For stable cross-repo scanners or validators, a Rust CLI can avoid per-repo Python environment drift.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: Agents default to Python scripts inside each repo because they are easy to write locally.
detection_signals: The same Python helper is copied across repos.
Validation fails because virtual environments or Python dependencies differ.
A tool does deterministic file scanning, hashing, or JSONL processing.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: A small pure parser or chunker boundary should often get a fuzz/property harness before it becomes a shared Rust tool.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: Agents often stop after table-driven examples pass and do not create adversarial input generation.
detection_signals: Rust code parses paths, JSONL, markdown, logs, mail packets, or registry records.
A function accepts bytes or strings from another repo or untrusted source.
A review finding mentions malformed input or panic risk.

ai_overlooked_patterns.summary: When Rust test speed or reliability matters, isolated runner evidence should precede claims that Rust made a workflow faster.
ai_overlooked_patterns.why_ai_may_miss_it: AI agents may compare a tiny Rust command to a full Python suite and miss scope or isolation differences.
detection_signals: A Rust timing claim lacks command, scope, exit code, and structured report evidence.
Rust tests share global state or pass locally but not in CI.
A parity harness needs per-test identity and duration records.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use Cargo metadata, cargo tree, and dependency audits to inspect the actual crate graph before adding or promoting Rust tooling.
run_or_inspect: cargo metadata --format-version 1 for workspace/package targets and feature surfaces.
cargo tree for dependency duplication, feature activation, and unexpected transitive crates.
cargo audit or RustSec review when security posture affects adoption.
use_when: A Rust tool, crate, or PyO3 extension is proposed for DAD or a downstream repo.
A build or packaging issue might be caused by features, target triples, or dependency drift.
proof_output: Workspace package IDs, enabled features, dependency-risk summary, and exact command results.
A license/provenance note before any crate becomes a DAD harness dependency.
safety_limits: Do not auto-upgrade or add crates by mail.
Do not publish private paths or internal crate names to public-facing repos without release review.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use cargo check, Clippy, rustfmt, doc tests, and rustdoc surfaces as executable proof, not optional polish.
run_or_inspect: cargo fmt --check.
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features with explicit lint exceptions.
cargo test --doc or cargo doc metadata when public APIs or examples changed.
use_when: Rust source changes touch public APIs, error types, invariants, or examples.
An AI agent needs the compiler and linter to carry part of the review burden.
proof_output: Command, exit code, warning/error class, and any intentionally allowed lint.
Doc-test or rustdoc evidence when examples are part of the contract.
safety_limits: Do not silence broad lint classes to make AI-generated Rust pass.
Do not claim compiler success proves behavioral parity with Python.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use structured Rust test identity and parity records before comparing Rust to Python or promoting a shadow replacement.
run_or_inspect: cargo test with captured command, exit code, and duration.
cargo nextest list/run when isolated runner evidence matters.
DAD rust-shadow-parity report comparing non-empty same-scope Python and Rust cases.
use_when: Rust is being evaluated as a shadow layer for Python behavior.
A speed claim could hide mismatched test scope.
proof_output: Per-command timings, test identities, report paths, parity map, and mismatch log.
Explicit coverage-unverified status when structured same-scope reports are missing.
safety_limits: Timing savings are not reportable when parity is failed or unverified.
Rust test success alone is not equivalent to Python native behavior.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use fuzz, property, mutation, or undefined-behavior checks as scouts for pure Rust boundaries before sharing the tool.
run_or_inspect: cargo fuzz, proptest, or quickcheck around pure parser/chunker/scanner functions.
cargo mutants as a candidate mutation-testing source when the crate and license are reviewed.
cargo miri for unsafe or interpreter-checkable undefined-behavior concerns.
use_when: Rust accepts untrusted text, bytes, source files, paths, JSONL, mail, or exception packets.
A parser, chunker, or classifier will become a DAD shared validator or scanner.
proof_output: Fuzz/property target name, generated-input policy, survived/killed mutation summary, or Miri result.
A sanitization note for any minimized failure case before it can leave the repo.
safety_limits: Do not mail generated corpora, private crash inputs, or raw source snippets.
Treat mutation and fuzz outcomes as harness evidence, not automatic proof of correctness.

ai_overlooked_operations.summary: Use API compatibility checks before Rust leaf tools become shared dependencies across repos.
run_or_inspect: cargo semver-checks as a candidate gate when a crate exposes a public Rust API.
Public API diff notes for binary or CLI tools whose output is consumed by agents.
Versioned JSON/report schema validation for Python-facing Rust CLIs.
use_when: A Rust crate or CLI becomes a DAD-owned shared asset.
Downstream repos may depend on the Rust output format, command flags, or library API.
proof_output: Compatibility command result, affected public items or output fields, and release-note pointer.
Human-reviewed migration note for breaking changes.
safety_limits: Do not treat API compatibility as semantic correctness.
Do not publish internal path examples in public release notes.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Use Rust enums, newtypes, typed errors, and exhaustive matches for closed states, IDs, packets, and route tables.
use_when: A boundary has a finite set of statuses, event types, parser states, or ID spaces.
Python or JSON string constants are being mirrored manually across files.
proof_required: The Rust API exposes typed variants rather than loose strings.
cargo test or compile failure demonstrates a new variant would force handler updates.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: The agent writes Rust that looks safe but still passes untyped strings and catch-all matches through the critical boundary.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Prefer one small Rust leaf tool or crate before any full platform rewrite.
use_when: A repo needs deterministic scanning, parsing, chunking, hashing, source-offset mapping, or single-binary validation.
Python environment drift is hurting cross-repo tooling.
proof_required: A narrow input/output contract and same-input tests exist.
The Python orchestration boundary remains stable unless human review approves broader movement.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: Rust spreads into orchestration, governance, and review surfaces before the first leaf tool has proved value.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Parser, chunker, scanner, and serializer boundaries that accept untrusted text or bytes need fuzz/property thinking before becoming shared tools.
use_when: Rust handles mail packets, JSONL, markdown, source text, logs, paths, or repo metadata.
A bug class involves malformed input, panic risk, truncation, or offset drift.
proof_required: A pure deterministic function can be fuzzed or property-tested.
Crash artifacts, corpora, and minimized cases stay local unless sanitized and approved.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: Examples pass, but adversarial inputs panic or corrupt offsets after the tool is shared across repos.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Rust speed claims require comparable scope, command identity, exit code, duration, and parity evidence.
use_when: A change claims Rust saves time versus Python.
A test runner, CLI, or shadow layer produces reports agents may use for promotion decisions.
proof_required: Native baseline and Rust command ran on the same workload or a declared equivalent map.
Structured reports prove non-empty same-scope coverage before timing is described as savings.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: A tiny Rust suite creates a false green and convinces DAD to promote a replacement that misses Python-only behavior.

agent_coding_guidelines.rule: Rust leaf tools should expose stable, schema-versioned machine outputs and narrow typed inputs that Python can validate independently.
use_when: A Rust scanner, chunker, parser, hasher, or validator will feed DAD or another repo.
A Rust CLI may later be reused, wrapped by Python, or compared against a native Python path.
proof_required: The Rust tool emits versioned JSON or JSONL with deterministic ordering and typed errors.
Python-side validation or parity tests can fail independently of Rust's own tests.
agent_coding_guidelines.failure_mode: Rust compiles and passes its own tests, but future agents cannot prove what changed, whether Python consumed the same scope, or whether downstream outputs stayed compatible.

Skipping Python native validation when a Rust extension exists.

intake_gate: Record pointer-only source refs, crate/tool version, license and maintenance notes, applicability limits, and a harness idea.

validation_gates: Profile before proposing Rust for speed.
Run Rust fmt, clippy, tests, and doc tests when Rust source changes.

adoption_rules: Prefer small Rust hot-path crates under stable Python-facing boundaries.

anti_patterns: Rust as prestige rewrite without measured bottleneck.
Tiny Rust suite treated as equivalent to broad Python tests.
Unsafe code or complex async introduced without an explicit need and review.
